title: Augmentation and transfer learning for images

videos.script: A hundred handwritten digits is not much to learn from. This lesson borrows more, in two ways. {{digit}} The first borrows from the images you already have. Turn a 6 a little, move it a pixel, and it is still a 6. {{jitter}} Each time the network sees it, the image is changed at random. Nothing extra is stored. {{batch}} But some changes lie. Turn a 6 upside down and it becomes a 9. {{sixnine}} A network trained with those lies gets worse, and you will measure by how much. {{table}} The second way borrows a whole network. Train one on the digits 0 to 4, and save it. {{pretrain}} Keep its body, put a new head on it, and teach it 5 to 9 from a few images. {{headswap}} Here the borrowing loses to a network trained from scratch. The run shows why. {{silent}} With a large donor, like a model trained on over a million photographs, the same move is how most image work starts. {{imagenet}} That download is shown, and not run here. {{end}}
